hero.title: Law in Mauritius
hero.subtitle: Studying **Law in Mauritius** can help students build a foundation in legal principles, legislation, legal research, advocacy, and dispute resolution. Students can choose an undergraduate Bachelor of Laws (LLB) or continue with a postgraduate Master of Laws (LLM) in a specialised area. **Law in Mauritius** offers undergraduate and postgraduate study pathways for students interested in legal education and related careers.

overview: For the 2026–2027 academic year, the University of Mauritius lists a three-year full-time LLB (Hons), a four-year part-time LLB (Hons), and postgraduate programmes in Corporate Law, Human Rights, and Business and Tax Law.

faq.question: Can I study Law in Mauritius after Class 12?
faq.answer: Yes. Students who meet the academic and language requirements can apply for an undergraduate LLB. The University of Mauritius lists a three-year full-time LLB (Hons), while Middlesex University Mauritius also offers a three-year full-time LLB (Hons). This makes a Bachelor's in Law in Mauritius an option for eligible students after Class 12\.

faq.question: How long does it take to complete an LLB in Mauritius?
faq.answer: The listed full-time LLB programmes at the University of Mauritius and Middlesex University Mauritius take three years. The University of Mauritius also lists a four-year part-time option.

faq.question: Which LLM specialisations are available in Mauritius?
faq.answer: The University of Mauritius lists postgraduate programmes in Corporate Law, Human Rights, and Business and Tax Law. Middlesex University Mauritius offers an LLM (General). Students should check the latest course information before applying. These options provide postgraduate pathways for students interested in a Master's in Law in Mauritius.

faq.question: What is the cost of studying Law in Mauritius?
faq.answer: For 2026–2027, Middlesex University Mauritius lists international tuition fees of £6,400 for its LLB (Hons) and £7,420 for its LLM (General). Accommodation, food, travel, and other expenses are additional.

faq.question: Can I practise as a lawyer after completing a Law degree in Mauritius?
faq.answer: Not automatically. Graduates must meet the professional training, eligibility, and registration requirements of the jurisdiction where they want to practise. Confirm the applicable pathway with the relevant legal professional body before choosing a programme. Choosing Law in Mauritius can provide students with undergraduate and postgraduate legal education options. Applicants should compare the available Law courses in Mauritius, verify university admission requirements and understand professional registration conditions before making their final decision.
